items.title: Physical crude prices top 2008 records as Hormuz blockade deepens

featured_image.name: Tankers showing caution around Strait of Hormuz after attack on Iran

items.description: European and Asian refiners are paying record prices of nearly $150 a barrel for physical crude oil cargoes, surpassing levels last seen during the 2008 financial crisis, as Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz continues to choke global supply.

items.title: North Korea fires projectile a day after rare diplomatic thaw

featured_image.name: Suspected North Korean missile launch 'failed,' possibly ...

items.description:
North Korea launched an unidentified projectile from its capital area on Tuesday, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff confirmed on Wednesday, in a move that came just one day after South Korean President Lee Jae Myung expressed regret over drone incursions into the North.[1][2]

The JCS said it detected the launch from the Pyongyang region and that South Korean and U.S. intelligence authorities are analyzing the projectile, without providing further details. The projectile, believed to have been fired in the morning, apparently failed shortly after launch, according to the Korea Times, citing Yonhap.[3][1]

items.title: Physical crude hits all-time high as Hormuz crisis deepens

featured_image.name: Strait Of Hormuz Standoff Threatens Global Oil Supply - Grand Pinnacle  Tribune

items.description:
The price of physical crude oil surged to all-time highs on Tuesday, with some grades nearing $150 a barrel as European and Asian refiners scrambled for immediate supply, underscoring the severity of the energy crisis triggered by the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.

Dated Brent, the benchmark used to price much of the world's physical crude, reached a record $144.42 per barrel on Tuesday afternoon, surpassing levels seen during both the 2008 financial crisis and Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, according to data compiled by S&P Global Platts. North Sea Forties crude climbed to $146.09 a barrel, also an all-time high, according to LSEG data. When the Platts dated Brent assessment is used as a base, many physical cargoes effectively priced above $150 a barrel.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: US and Iran set for pivotal peace talks Friday in Islamabad

featured_image.name: US, Iran to pause war, agree to 2-week ceasefire

items.description:
Iran's Supreme National Security Council confirmed that formal negotiations with the United States will begin on Friday, April 10, in Islamabad, following a dramatic two-week ceasefire announced by President Donald Trump on Tuesday evening just 90 minutes before his own deadline to launch devastating strikes on Iranian infrastructure.[1][2][3]

The SNSC, in a statement posted to its Telegram channel, said Iran would enter the talks with "complete distrust of the American side" and stressed that agreeing to negotiate "does not mean the end of the war". Iran has allocated up to two weeks for the negotiations, with the possibility of extension by mutual agreement.[4][5]

items.title: Dated Brent surges to record $144 as Iran war chokes supply

featured_image.name: Dated Brent Oil Price Jumps to Highest Level on Record ...

items.description:
Physical oil prices hit an all-time high on Tuesday as the war in Iran, now in its sixth week, continues to choke global crude supply through the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Dated Brent, the benchmark for North Sea crude bought and sold for near-term delivery, soared above $144 a barrel — the highest level since the pricing series began in 1987, according to Bloomberg.[1][2]

The record in physical prices underscores the growing desperation among refiners scrambling to secure barrels for immediate delivery, even as Brent futures for June settled lower near $109 a barrel on Tuesday. The widening gap between spot and futures prices reflects a market where traders are paying steep premiums for crude they can get their hands on now.[1]

items.title: Oil prices drop as Pakistan-brokered ceasefire pauses US-Iran strikes

featured_image.name: U.S. oil price plunges 14% to below $100 after Trump agrees to two-week ceasefire in Iran war

items.description: Six weeks of war between the United States and Iran have sent oil prices soaring past $100 a barrel, fueling the sharpest inflation fears since 2023 and forcing the Federal Reserve into a holding pattern on interest rates. On Tuesday, a last-minute two-week ceasefire brokered by Pakistan offered a glimmer of relief — crude prices dropped sharply in evening trading — but economists warn the damage to consumer confidence and the inflation outlook may already be done.

items.title: Afghanistan calls China-brokered talks with Pakistan 'useful'

featured_image.name: Afghanistan, Pakistan hold 'useful' peace talks in China, says Kabul |  Reuters

items.description: Afghanistan's Taliban-led government on Tuesday described ongoing peace talks with Pakistan in China as "useful," even as Pakistan's military chief vowed to press forward with military operations against militant targets on Afghan soil, underscoring the fragility of the diplomatic effort.

items.title: Iran accepts two-week ceasefire hours before Trump's deadline to strike

featured_image.name: Trump suspends Iran attack for two weeks, subject to Hormuz Strait ...

items.description:
Iran's Supreme National Security Council on Tuesday confirmed it had accepted a two-week ceasefire in its war with the United States, the Associated Press reported, pulling the two nations back from the brink of a catastrophic escalation just hours after President Donald Trump warned that "a whole civilization will die tonight" if Tehran did not capitulate to his demands.[1][2]

The announcement came shortly before Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern deadline expired, capping a day of extreme brinkmanship in which U.S. forces struck military targets on Iran's Kharg Island oil export hub and Israeli warplanes hit bridges and railway infrastructure across the country.[3][4]

items.title: Trump suspends Iran strikes for two weeks, citing progress on peace deal

featured_image.name: White House Trump Briefing

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced on Tuesday evening that he would suspend U.S. military strikes on Iran for two weeks, pulling back from his threat to destroy the country's power plants and bridges just 88 minutes before his self-imposed 8 p.m. ET deadline. The announcement, posted on Truth Social at 6:32 p.m. ET, came after a day in which Trump had warned that "a whole civilization will die tonight" if Iran did not agree to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.[1][2]

"Based on conversations with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir, of Pakistan, and wherein they requested that I hold off the destructive force being sent tonight to Iran, and subject to the Islamic Republic of Iran agreeing to the COMPLETE, IMMEDIATE, and SAFE OPENING of the Strait of Hormuz, I agree to suspend the bombing and attack of Iran for a period of two weeks," Trump wrote.[2][3]

items.title: Trump agrees to two-week Iran ceasefire hours before strike deadline

featured_image.name: Trump deadline for Iran ticks closer as Islamic republic rejects temporary ceasefire

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced on Tuesday evening that he would suspend planned military strikes against Iran for two weeks, calling the arrangement a "double-sided ceasefire" just hours after warning that "a whole civilization will die tonight" if no deal was reached by his 8 p.m. ET deadline. The pause is conditional on Iran agreeing to the "complete, immediate, and safe opening" of the Strait of Hormuz, with Trump citing a 10-point proposal from Tehran as a "workable basis" for negotiations toward a longer-term peace agreement.[1][2]

The announcement followed a last-minute diplomatic push by Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who publicly urged Trump on X to extend his deadline by two weeks "to allow diplomacy to run its course". Sharif also called on Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz during the same period "as a goodwill gesture". Pakistan's Field Marshal Asim Munir, whom Trump has previously called his "favourite" field marshal, had been in communication overnight with U.S. Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff, as well as Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: Trump confirms 'heated negotiations' as Iran deadline nears

featured_image.name: Trump warns Iran’s ‘whole civilization will die tonight’ unless deal struck

items.description:
With hours remaining before President Trump's self-imposed 8 p.m. Eastern deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, the president confirmed that the United States was engaged in active talks with Tehran but refused to share details. "We're in heated negotiations," Trump told Fox News in a phone call, declining to say how he felt about the discussions.[1][2]

The disclosure came as Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif made a last-ditch appeal for more time, posting on X that he "earnestly" requested Trump extend his deadline by two weeks. Sharif asked Iran to reopen the strait during that same period "as a goodwill gesture" and called on "all warring parties to observe a ceasefire everywhere for two weeks to allow diplomacy to achieve conclusive termination of war." White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed Trump "has been made aware of the proposal, and a response will come," according to CBS News and ABC News. A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran was "positively reviewing" the Pakistani proposal.[3][4][5][1]

items.title: Iran fires cluster munitions at central Israel as war enters sixth week

featured_image.name: Iran launches waves of missiles at Israel in response to attacks

items.description: Iran launched multiple ballistic missile barrages targeting Israeli cities on Tuesday, with cluster munitions striking areas across central Israel and causing widespread property damage, though Israeli emergency services reported no fatalities from the day's attacks.

items.title: US, Israel strike Iran's largest aluminum plant

featured_image.name: Trump deadline for Iran ticks closer as Islamic republic rejects temporary ...

items.description: American and Israeli forces struck the Iran Aluminium Company (IRALCO) in Arak on Tuesday, targeting the country's largest aluminum producer and sparking a major fire at the facility, as President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz drew near. The strike marks a further expansion of the five-week US-Israeli air campaign into Iran's core industrial base, following earlier attacks on steel mills, petrochemical complexes, and nuclear sites.

items.title: Iranians form human chains around power plants as energy strikes loom

featured_image.name: Iranians 'form human chains' at power plants: state media

items.description: As President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. ET deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached on Tuesday, Iranian authorities launched a nationwide campaign calling on young people to form "human chains" around the country's power plants and energy infrastructure in a dramatic act of defiance.

items.title: Iranians form human chains at power plants as energy strikes loom

featured_image.name: Iranians begin forming human chains around power plants ahead of ...

items.description: As President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. ET deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached on Tuesday, Iranian authorities launched a nationwide campaign calling on young people to form "human chains" around power plants and other critical infrastructure in a bid to deter threatened American strikes.

items.title: IDF warns of rising Iranian missile fire as Trump's deadline nears

featured_image.name: What are Iran’s cluster munitions that are penetrating Israeli defences?

items.description:
The Israel Defense Forces warned late Tuesday that missile fire toward Israeli territory could intensify "in the coming hours" as President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached with no deal in sight.[1][2]

In a statement, the IDF urged the public to "remain vigilant, alert, and act responsibly, while continuing to follow the Home Front Command's instructions". The warning came as Iran fired fresh salvos of ballistic missiles at central and southern Israel on Tuesday, with cluster munitions striking multiple locations in the Sharon plain, according to the IDF. Earlier in the day, the military had urged Iranians to avoid train travel nationwide, before confirming strikes on a railway bridge in Kashan that killed at least two people.[3][4][2][5]

items.title: Trump sets 8 p.m. deadline for Iran to reopen Hormuz

featured_image.name: Trump issues expletive-laden threat to Iran demanding Strait of Hormuz be  opened - BBC News

items.description:
More than five weeks after the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran on February 28, the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to most commercial shipping, triggering what the International Energy Agency has called the "largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market." On Tuesday, President Donald Trump set an 8 p.m. ET deadline for Iran to reopen the strait or face the destruction of its power plants and civilian infrastructure, posting on social media that "a whole civilization will die tonight."[1][2][3]

The narrow waterway between Iran and Oman normally carries roughly 20% of global oil trade and a similar share of liquefied natural gas shipments. Since the conflict began, daily vessel crossings have plummeted by more than 90%, from an average of 138 ships per day to single digits, according to Goldman Sachs, which warned that countries could soon face outright oil shortages. Iran has maintained a selective passage regime, exporting its own oil while permitting transit only to nations that "pay a toll" and denying access to all others.[4][5][6][7]

items.title: Pakistan's Sharif urges Trump to extend Iran deadline two weeks

featured_image.name: Trump extends deadline for Iran to reopen oil route or face ... - PBS

items.description:
Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday called on President Donald Trump to extend his deadline for Iran by two weeks, issuing a public plea just hours before Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern time ultimatum that has threatened devastating strikes on Iranian power plants and bridges.

"I earnestly request President Trump to extend the deadline for two weeks," Sharif wrote in a message posted on X, according to The Wall Street Journal. He also called on Tehran to temporarily reopen the Strait of Hormuz for the same two-week period "as a sign of goodwill," and urged all warring parties to observe a ceasefire across all fronts to allow diplomacy to produce a lasting resolution.[1][2]

items.title: White House denies nuclear strike plans as Iran deadline looms

featured_image.name: White House rejects claims Vance remarks hinted at Iran ...

items.description: The White House on Tuesday forcefully denied that Vice President JD Vance had suggested the United States might use nuclear weapons against Iran, after his remarks about unused military options fueled widespread speculation amid escalating tensions over President Donald Trump's latest deadline for Tehran.

items.title: Kuwait orders residents indoors as Trump's Iran deadline looms

featured_image.name: Kuwait Is Set to Allow Banks to Offer Mortgages for the First Time

items.description: Kuwait's Ministry of Interior on Tuesday urged all citizens and residents to stay home and avoid going outdoors from midnight to 6:00 a.m. on Wednesday, April 8, citing precautionary security measures as regional tensions reach a critical juncture. The directive, described as a "precautionary measure," comes as President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approaches Tuesday evening, with the president warning of devastating strikes on Iranian infrastructure if no deal is reached.[1][2][3][4]
